newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW- Fujitsu to double Asia telecom sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW- Fujitsu to double Asia telecom sales.

text.p: Japan's Fujitsu Ltd aims to double its sales of telecommunications and information products in the booming Asia market in the 1997/98 business year, president Tadashi Sekizawa told Reuters on Wednesday.

"We lost out to Europeans and Americans in the first stage of the battle (in Asia's telecom market)," Sekizawa said in an interview, referring to the overwhelming strength U.S. and European makers enjoy in Asia's cellular phone market.
"But there is a chance in new business areas, where traditional ties with American and European makers are weak, and we actually plan to sell everything we have in these fields." Sekizawa said.

Fujitsu, which recently surprised the Japanese stock market with a bullish outlook, expects sales of telecommunications and information products to jump 48 percent to 95 billion yen in Asia in the year to end-March 1998, a Fujitsu spokeswoman said.
Fujitsu, strong in network building, expects group net profit to double in the 1997/98 year ending March 31.
A company spokesman said it expected to benefit from Japanese makers' aggressive investments in personal computers, servers, mainframes, software and telecommunications equipment.

In China, Fujitsu is now the second biggest digital switching system maker, with a 12 percent share, after Alcatel, which holds a 43 percent share of the market, Sekizawa said at the Asia Telecom 97 trade fair.

In addition to switching systems, ATM next-generation switches and optic fibre systems, Fujitsu will launch a computer systems support business in Asia this year to help corporate clients build local call networks, Sekizawa said.
It plans to lease large-capacity, 1.5 megabit/bps cables from a global telecommunications alliance to offer systems support services, he said.
Sekizawa also said Singapore would become a hub for its emerging new businesses such as construction and maintenance of networks and development of software.
